entries.title: Release 26.10.1-alpha.31 — Ken's Actual fork
entries.body:
**Unofficial fork prerelease.** Based on upstream Actual v26.11.0 (`1766241e3f4b3c578e424c4fa15f1eb83c0da17d`, October 29, 2026); not an official Actual Budget release.

This release fixes the app hanging on "Loading global preferences..." after you sign out with an identity provider, and makes every refused OpenID sign-in log its reason.
entries.details:
#### Features

- None.

#### Enhancements

- None.

#### Bugfixes

- After signing out with an identity provider, the app no longer hangs on "Loading global preferences..." and lands on the sign-in page instead.

#### Maintenance

- The sync server now logs a reason for every refused OpenID sign-in, and escapes provider-supplied values so they can't forge log lines.
- Specifications now pass strict validation, and Fork CI enforces it.
- No upstream changes in this release; the fork stays on upstream Actual 26.11.0.

#### Known limitations

- Experimental.
- Tapping a tag in the transaction editor does nothing.
- Tags are not yet fully accessible on the phone.
- OpenID sign-out needs the server's address in the identity provider's allowed sign-out addresses; without it the provider shows an error page, though you are already signed out of Actual.
- Attached documents aren't included in a budget export, and removed documents stay on the sync server.
- HEIC pictures are refused; use the Photos library or a JPEG or PNG copy.
- Attaching a document needs a connection; there is no offline upload queue.
- No iPhone acceptance test is claimed.

entries.title: Release 26.10.1-alpha.26 — Ken's Actual fork
entries.body:
**Unofficial fork prerelease.** Based on upstream Actual `master` at `21c2b3f703142f858af4c653a31e675ca5ff85d7` (October 26, 2026), which comes after Actual 26.10.0 and is not itself an upstream release; not an official Actual Budget release.

This release lets you attach documents such as receipts to transactions, on desktop and on the phone, and brings the experimental Amazon order import to the phone.
entries.details:
#### Features

- Attach documents to transactions on desktop. A PDF, JPEG, PNG or WebP file can be attached to a saved transaction, then opened or removed (with Undo); a paperclip marks transactions that have documents. Documents are stored on the sync server, encrypted with the budget's key when the budget is encrypted, up to 10 MB each and 1 GB per budget by default. Attaching needs a sync server.
- Attach documents on the phone. The transaction screen has a Documents section: attach from Files, the camera or the Photos library, open a document inside the app and share or save it, or remove it with Undo. Rows with documents show a paperclip.
- Experimental Amazon order itemization on the phone. With **Amazon order itemization** turned on under **Settings > Experimental features**, the **All accounts** menu offers **Import Amazon orders**; review the matched charges and apply them one at a time or all at once, with Undo.

#### Enhancements

- Merging two transactions keeps the documents attached to either one, and deleting a transaction removes its documents from the budget.
- Changing the encryption key re-encrypts attached documents with the new key.

#### Bugfixes

- None.

#### Maintenance

- The sync server has new settings `ACTUAL_ATTACHMENTS_FILE_SIZE_LIMIT_MB` (default 10) and `ACTUAL_ATTACHMENTS_BUDGET_QUOTA_MB` (default 1024), and `/info` reports the per-document limit.
- OpenSpec records for transaction attachments on desktop and phone and for the phone Amazon import; agent docs record that every user-facing feature ships on desktop and on the phone.
- The MCP coverage list records that attachments are not MCP tools yet.
- The mobile Settings screenshots used by the visual tests are updated for the new export notice.

#### Known limitations

- Experimental.
- Upstream changes made after 26.10.0 have not yet been through an upstream release.
- Attached documents aren't included in a budget export, and removed documents stay on the sync server.
- HEIC pictures are refused; use the Photos library or a JPEG or PNG copy.
- Attaching a document needs a connection; there is no offline upload queue.
- No iPhone acceptance test is claimed.

entries.title: Release 26.10.1-alpha.25 — Ken's Actual fork
entries.body:
**Unofficial fork prerelease.** Based on upstream Actual `master` at `21c2b3f703142f858af4c653a31e675ca5ff85d7` (October 26, 2026), which comes after Actual 26.10.0 and is not itself an upstream release; not an official Actual Budget release.

This release adds experimental Amazon order itemization, and is the first build whose release also carries the hosted MCP container image, so the read-write hosted MCP from 26.10.1-alpha.24 can be deployed with it.
entries.details:
#### Features

- Experimental Amazon order itemization. Turn on **Amazon order itemization** under **Settings > Experimental features**, then choose **Import Amazon orders** from the **All accounts** menu and pick Amazon's order-history CSV file. Actual matches each card charge to a transaction of the same amount near the ship date, lets you review the matches, and on **Apply selected** splits each charge into one line per item (or, for a single item, writes the item name into the notes). Lines get their category from your rules where a rule sets one. The file is read on your device and not kept. Desktop only.

#### Enhancements

- None.

#### Bugfixes

- None.

#### Maintenance

- The release build also produces the hosted MCP container image, and the deploy loads and checks it on the server, so the MCP image no longer has to be built and loaded by hand. This takes effect once the updated deploy command is installed on the server.
- Documentation for Amazon order itemization, and its OpenSpec records.
- The MCP coverage list records that the Amazon import is used from the app, not through MCP tools.

#### Known limitations

- Experimental.
- Upstream changes made after 26.10.0 have not yet been through an upstream release.
- Amazon order itemization does not handle refunds or returns, orders paid partly by a gift card or points, or off-budget accounts.
- The stdio MCP server still runs on your own computer and needs Node.js 22 or later and the 1Password CLI.
- No iPhone acceptance test is claimed.

This release lets the hosted assistant connector change your budget, not only read it, on staging and on production.
entries.details:
#### Features

- The hosted MCP entry (`actual-mcp-http`) is now read-write. It offers the same `write_` tools as the stdio `--writes` entry, with the same limits, and logs each write first to `<data folder>.audit.jsonl` (`production-remote.audit.jsonl` on production) with the caller's OAuth subject. A production host is still served only under the production guard.

#### Enhancements

- The stdio MCP server's `--writes` entry can now be used against a production host when `ACTUAL_MCP_ALLOW_PRODUCTION=1` is set.
- The `sync_budget` tool also sends the local copy's changes where write tools are offered, as the app does.
- The hosted entry's OAuth metadata names the resource "Actual Budget" instead of "Actual Budget (read-only)".

#### Bugfixes

- None.

#### Maintenance

- OpenSpec records for the read-write hosted entry, the shared Auth0 tenant for production identities, the shorter production go-live path and the Amazon order itemization layout.
- Agent hooks also block agents from approving deployments, including through the GraphQL API.
- The MCP README describes the read-write hosted entry.

#### Known limitations

- Experimental.
- Upstream changes made after 26.10.0 have not yet been through an upstream release.
- The hosted MCP container image is built and loaded on the server by hand; it is not part of this release's Docker image.

entries.title: Release 26.10.1-alpha.23 — Ken's Actual fork
entries.body:
**Unofficial fork prerelease.** Based on upstream Actual `master` at `21c2b3f703142f858af4c653a31e675ca5ff85d7` (October 26, 2026), which comes after Actual 26.10.0 and is not itself an upstream release; not an official Actual Budget release.

This release lets a server owner require that the first OpenID sign-in is a named person, refuses an empty OpenID identity, and tightens the rate limits and start-up checks of the hosted MCP entry. The hosted MCP entry is still not deployed anywhere.
entries.details:
#### Features

- A new, optional setting, `ACTUAL_OPENID_ADMIN_SUBJECT`, names the provider subject (`sub`) that the first OpenID sign-in must have. When it is set, a first sign-in from any other identity is refused, so the first person to reach the sign-in page cannot become the administrator. Unset, the server behaves as upstream does: the first OpenID identity becomes the administrator, and the server logs a warning at start-up.
- The hosted MCP entry can serve a production host, read-only, but only when `ACTUAL_MCP_REMOTE_PRODUCTION=1` is set and the production guard is met: a session token file and no password, a provider subject (not an email address) as the allowed account, the data folder `production-remote`, and a token that belongs to a user who is not an administrator. Otherwise it still refuses a production host. It is not deployed anywhere yet.

#### Enhancements

- The hosted MCP entry limits its OAuth endpoints per source address and adds a ceiling over each /24 (IPv4) or /48 (IPv6) group of sources, set with `ACTUAL_MCP_RATE_PER_PREFIX` (default 600 per window). A request to `/mcp` with a valid token counts only against the per-client limit.
- The hosted MCP entry refuses to start with a loopback server address unless it also listens on loopback.
- The MCP image build leaves local `.env` files (`.env`, `.env.local` and `.env.*.local`) out of its build context.

#### Bugfixes

- The sync server now refuses an OpenID sign-in whose identity is empty. Upstream would have matched an empty identity to the password-method user. This fixes a flaw in upstream's code; it is fixed here only.
- When `ACTUAL_OPENID_ADMIN_SUBJECT` is set, the sync server also refuses a sign-in whose ID-token `sub` differs from the user-info `sub`.

#### Maintenance

- OpenSpec records for the production identities (the production sync server uses an Auth0 tenant) and for the hosted MCP entry serving production under an explicit guard.
- The MCP README documents the new settings.

#### Known limitations

- Experimental.
- Upstream changes made after 26.10.0 have not yet been through an upstream release.
- The hosted MCP entry is not deployed anywhere yet. It is read-only, and it still refuses a production host unless the production guard above is met.
- `ACTUAL_OPENID_ADMIN_SUBJECT` only affects the first sign-in; it does not change an administrator that already exists.
- The stdio MCP server still runs on your own computer and needs Node.js 22 or later and the 1Password CLI.
- No iPhone acceptance test is claimed.

entries.title: Release 26.10.1-alpha.22 — Ken's Actual fork
entries.body:
**Unofficial fork prerelease.** Based on upstream Actual `master` at `21c2b3f703142f858af4c653a31e675ca5ff85d7` (October 26, 2026), which comes after Actual 26.10.0 and is not itself an upstream release; not an official Actual Budget release.

This release adds a hosted, read-only entry for the MCP server, a content-free access log for the sync server, and a clearer record of who acted through the MCP server.
entries.details:
#### Features

- The MCP server has a hosted, read-only entry that serves the Model Context Protocol over streamable HTTP, with sync freshness checks and rate limits. It includes an OAuth provider and token store, so only the one configured account can sign in through the identity provider. It serves staging only, refuses a production host even with the override, and is not deployed by this release.

#### Enhancements

- Every MCP audit line records the sync-server user id and the OAuth subject (`local` on stdio).
- The MCP server can sign in with a session token read from a file that only its owner can read (mode 0400).
- The sync server writes a content-free access log (no budget content, no passwords) and ships a runbook for keeping it off the host.
- The sync server logs access decisions on every file route, and new uploads.
- The hosted MCP entry carries the verified OAuth subject on its access lines, requires a long client secret, and refuses loopback redirects.

#### Bugfixes

- None in this release.

#### Maintenance

- Documentation for the hosted MCP identity provider (Auth0 as the example) and what any provider must support.
- OpenSpec records for the production-identities design and the OpenID staging rehearsal findings.
- The `actual-mcp-http` command is recorded in `yarn.lock`.

#### Known limitations

- Experimental.
- Upstream changes made after 26.10.0 have not yet been through an upstream release.
- The hosted MCP entry is not deployed anywhere yet. It serves staging only and refuses a production host even with the override. It is read-only; production is unchanged.
- The stdio MCP server still runs on your own computer and needs Node.js 22 or later and the 1Password CLI.
- No iPhone acceptance test is claimed.

entries.title: Release 26.10.1-alpha.21 — Ken's Actual fork
entries.body:
**Unofficial fork prerelease.** Based on upstream Actual `master` at `21c2b3f703142f858af4c653a31e675ca5ff85d7` (October 26, 2026), which comes after Actual 26.10.0 and is not itself an upstream release; not an official Actual Budget release.

This release adds an MCP server, so an AI assistant on your computer can look up your budget; it is read-only unless you turn on writes. It also adds a Notifications row to the phone Settings list and fixes several schedule, Move on budget and release-news details.
entries.details:
#### Features

- An MCP server (`@actual-app/mcp`) lets an AI assistant that speaks the Model Context Protocol, such as Claude Code or Claude Desktop, look up accounts, categories, payees, transactions, budget months, schedules, paychecks and business calendars in your budget. It is **read-only by default**: it starts the budget engine read-only, so it sends nothing to the server. It talks to the assistant over standard input and output and opens no network port.
  - To install and run it, follow the "MCP Server" page in the API docs (`api/mcp-server`): build it from this release's tag with `yarn build:mcp`, keep the server password in 1Password and pass it with `op run`, and register the server with your assistant.
  - Changes are opt-in: a separate entry started with `--writes` adds tools to create transactions, change a transaction's category, payee or notes, set a budget amount, skip a paycheck and move an account on budget. Each change is recorded in a private audit log before it runs. `--writes` is never allowed for production.

#### Enhancements

- The MCP server's `get_budget_month` returns a budget month page by page by category, with the whole month's totals and the category count on every page.
- On a phone, Settings has a Notifications row that shows how many entries are unseen, and the Notifications page has a Back button.
- The API has methods for paychecks, business calendars and moving accounts on budget, and names `updatePaycheck` when a script tries to edit a paycheck's schedule.
- The API's `init` takes a `readOnly` option, so a session writes and pushes nothing.

#### Bugfixes

- A schedule form error shows once, instead of also appearing as "Could not search" in the empty transactions list.
- Choosing a date relative to another schedule no longer shows a "Could not search" error before a schedule is chosen.
- When the start date in "Move on budget" is cleared or isn't a real date, the old preview is hidden and a "Choose a start date" hint shows.
- On a phone, the "Categorize moved history?" title shows in full instead of being cut off.
- Fork release cards label their link "View release notes on GitHub" instead of "View on actualbudget.org".
- A release's category counts no longer count the "None in this release." placeholder as a change.
- Two dependencies used by the server are updated to versions that fix reported security issues.
- The MCP server checks its data folder before creating it, so an unsafe location (for example a synced folder) is refused before anything is written there.
- The MCP server's `--writes` entry keeps its own copy of the budget, separate from the read entry's, so a write that hasn't synced yet never sits in the copy a read session uses. **If you used the MCP server before this release:** if you ever ran a write session with the read folder, stop the read entry and delete that folder once (for example `rm -r "$HOME/Library/Application Support/actual-mcp/staging"`); the next read start downloads a clean copy. See the MCP server's README.
- The MCP server's read tools clean untrusted paycheck text, page the transfers in the Move on budget preview, and report "No matching date" for a repeat rule that never matches.

#### Maintenance

- The MCP server is released as the eighth version-aligned package, and a check fails the build when the eight versions drift.
- The MCP server's tool list is checked against the API's handlers, so a new handler can't ship without a tool decision.
- Agent workflow, branch-protection and OpenSpec housekeeping.

#### Known limitations

- Experimental.
- Upstream changes made after 26.10.0 have not yet been through an upstream release.
- The MCP server runs on your own computer; it is not installed on the server. It needs Node.js 22 or later and the 1Password CLI.
- Each deposit must go to a different account, and every paycheck repeats its defined amounts; edit a posted transaction for a one-off change.
- Imported deposits more than about 7.5% from the expected amount do not link automatically.
- A duplicate of the latest paycheck (for example, imported twice) can hide the next skipped date.
- Releases published on the same day may show the "What's new" message for any of them; the Notifications page lists all.
- No iPhone acceptance test is claimed.

entries.title: Release 26.10.1-alpha.19 — Ken's Actual fork
entries.body:
**Unofficial fork prerelease.** Based on upstream Actual `master` at `21c2b3f703142f858af4c653a31e675ca5ff85d7` (October 26, 2026), which comes after Actual 26.10.0 and is not itself an upstream release; not an official Actual Budget release.

This release lets you move an off-budget account on budget, keeps paycheck schedules consistent after edits on several devices, shows skipped dates in paycheck and schedule editors, and makes secondary and warning text easier to read in every theme. Paycheck and business calendar screens work better on a phone.
entries.details:
#### Features

- Move an off-budget account on budget from its account menu, on desktop and on a phone. You pick the start date, see the starting balance first, and can undo the move. An invalid start date is refused.

#### Enhancements

- Transactions from before an account moved on budget show as moved history instead of uncategorized, and Actual asks before you categorize them.
- Secondary and warning text is easier to read in every theme.
- The clearing-account note and the paycheck schedule note are easier to read in every theme.
- On a phone, the paycheck editor stacks the deduction and deposit fields, each with a short visible label.
- On a phone, deleting a paycheck or a business calendar uses the same delete sheet as the rest of the app.
- Deleting a business calendar names the calendar and says what deleting it changes.

#### Bugfixes

- Paycheck schedules are reconciled after edits made on several devices at once, so they no longer drift apart.
- "Upcoming dates" in schedule and paycheck editors start from the schedule's next date, so skipped dates show.
- A goal template for a schedule dated relative to another schedule keeps working after the schedule it follows is deleted.
- Deleting a paycheck on a phone returns to Schedules.

#### Maintenance

- Pages that show schedule dates share one schedules query instead of each running its own.
- The web worker no longer bundles an unused cryptography library.
- A development-only dependency advisory (`qs`) is resolved.
- Fork checks now run on every merged commit on `development`, so the combined result is tested, not only each pull request.
- A nightly report runs mutation tests on the shared date and money code and lists spec scenarios that no test names.
- Phone page-heading tests catch text that is clipped sideways as well as vertically.
- A test fixture uses placeholder names.

#### Known limitations

- Experimental.
- Upstream changes made after 26.10.0 have not yet been through an upstream release.
- Each deposit must go to a different account, and every paycheck repeats its defined amounts; edit a posted transaction for a one-off change.
- Imported deposits more than about 7.5% from the expected amount do not link automatically.
- A duplicate of the latest paycheck (for example, imported twice) can hide the next skipped date.
- Goal templates already applied under alpha.17 keep their amounts until templates are applied again.
- Each device's own sign-in limit (from alpha.18) takes effect only after the server's proxy setting is updated; until then, one device's failed sign-ins can still lock out others.
- Releases published on the same day may show the "What's new" message for any of them; the Notifications page lists all.
- No iPhone acceptance test is claimed.

entries.body:
**Unofficial fork prerelease.** Based on upstream Actual `master` at `21c2b3f703142f858af4c653a31e675ca5ff85d7` (October 26, 2026), which comes after Actual 26.10.0 and is not itself an upstream release; not an official Actual Budget release.

This release fixes a way to crash the sync server before signing in, stops one device's failed sign-ins from locking out the family's other devices, and fixes several schedule problems: schedules dated relative to another schedule now move on after they're paid or posted, goal templates budget every occurrence of them, paychecks show their upcoming and skipped dates again, and Business calendars stays on while you have paychecks. Paycheck, calendar and clearing-account screens work better on a phone.
entries.details:
#### Features

- None in this release.

#### Enhancements

- Choose an account's business calendar on a phone, as on desktop.
- The API refuses to edit or delete schedules that a paycheck created, so a script can't break a paycheck by accident.
- Clearing accounts are marked on a phone too, and a paycheck whose deposit is late shows the clearing-account warning there.
- Paycheck screens on a phone have larger touch targets, a clearly marked Delete, and dates that match desktop.
- Business calendar screens on a phone have larger touch targets, a clearly marked Delete, a Save button that stays in view, and presets set apart from your own dates.
- Business calendars can't be turned off while the budget has paychecks, because paychecks use them; a note in Settings > Experimental explains why, and screen readers read it out. The toggle also stays locked while paychecks are still loading. With no paychecks, turning Business calendars off also turns Paychecks off. If your budget has paychecks but business calendars are turned off, Paychecks now starts off too. Turn on Paychecks in Settings > Experimental to see them again.

#### Bugfixes

- A specially crafted compressed request can no longer crash the sync server before anyone signs in.
- One device's failed sign-ins no longer lock out the family's other devices; each device has its own limit.
- Schedule previews and next dates update as soon as a business calendar change syncs in from another device.
- A schedule dated relative to another schedule moves to its next date after it is paid or automatically posted, instead of staying on the old date. Schedules stuck on alpha.17 catch up the next time Actual checks schedules on each device (once a day, after a sync): any occurrences missed since then are posted. Check for deposits you entered yourself meanwhile.
- A goal template for a schedule dated relative to another schedule budgets every occurrence in the month, not just one.
- A schedule dated relative to a one-time schedule is completed once its only occurrence is paid or posted, like a one-time schedule, instead of staying open.
- Paychecks show "Show more" and their skipped dates again, rules name the schedule a relative date follows, and screens that move dates to business days use the right calendar.
- The phone Back button is easier to tap.
- A long page title in a phone header ends with an ellipsis instead of being cut off.

#### Maintenance

- Tests cover relative dates in goal templates and forecasts, schedule business-day scenarios, and paycheck frequency changes, same-day holiday deposits and the hidden menu.
- The client version test finds the version in the redesigned Settings.
- Fork checks build the app and run the mobile browser tests before changes merge, and type checks no longer fail at random on a first run.
- A rules test waits for a renamed schedule to sync, instead of failing at random.
- Paycheck and preview tests use stable mocks and no longer time out under load.
- Closing a budget waits for a running schedule check to finish, so a script that syncs and closes straight away no longer crashes.

#### Known limitations

- Experimental.
- Upstream changes made after 26.10.0 have not yet been through an upstream release.
- "Upcoming dates" in schedule and paycheck editors does not reflect skipped dates.
- Each deposit must go to a different account, and every paycheck repeats its defined amounts; edit a posted transaction for a one-off change.
- Imported deposits more than about 7.5% from the expected amount do not link automatically.
- A duplicate of the latest paycheck (for example, imported twice) can hide the next skipped date.
- The mobile business calendar editor uses the desktop editor's layout.
- Goal templates already applied under alpha.17 keep their amounts until templates are applied again.
- Releases published on the same day may show the "What's new" message for any of them; the Notifications page lists all.
- Synthetic staging only; no real financial data or production paperwork migration. No iPhone acceptance test is claimed.

- The API's schedule dates (`getScheduleDates`) also work for a date relative to another schedule.

#### Bugfixes

- A new or re-dated pay schedule no longer counts older paychecks linked to it, so its first skipped paydays show as "Skipped".
- From upstream: 73 bug fixes, including keeping sign-in and bank connection credentials out of server request logs, preventing bank sync credentials from being reused after a budget is deleted, not leaving a budget file half-written when saving fails, and posting a schedule created or edited later on the day it is due.

#### Maintenance

- From upstream: dependency updates, Node.js 24.22.1 and stricter React Compiler lint rules. Three fork hooks were reworked to follow those rules.
- Tests cover relative dates in the API's schedule dates, and paychecks with history from before their pay schedule started.

#### Known limitations

- Experimental.
- Upstream changes made after 26.10.0 have not yet been through an upstream release.
- "Upcoming dates" in schedule and paycheck editors does not reflect skipped dates.
- Each deposit must go to a different account, and every paycheck repeats its defined amounts; edit a posted transaction for a one-off change.

Paychecks get their own section on the Schedules page and can be edited on a phone, clearing accounts warn when they don't empty, holidays can follow Easter, and business calendars can be managed on a phone.
entries.details:
#### Features

- The Schedules page has a Paychecks section at the top, on desktop and mobile. Each paycheck shows its next pay date, net pay and where each deposit goes. You can skip the next paycheck (and undo it), see skipped dates, open a paycheck to edit it, or add one. A paycheck's own schedules no longer clutter the schedules list.
- Paychecks can be created, edited, skipped and deleted on a phone, on a single scrolling page with net pay and Save always in view.
- Business calendars can be managed on a phone: the Schedules page links to a list of calendars, and each calendar opens in a full-page editor. Deleting a calendar asks first.
- Business calendar holidays can be set relative to Easter Sunday (for example, Good Friday is 2 days before), so they no longer need a new exception every year.

#### Enhancements

- An account that a paycheck uses for clearing shows a paycheck icon in the sidebar and a note at the top of its register saying it should return to zero after each payday.
- When a clearing account still has a balance and a deposit is more than 2 business days late, its register and the paycheck's row on the Schedules page warn, with the balance and the deposits that haven't arrived.
- The Easter offset field explains when its value isn't a whole number from -100 to 100 and won't save until it is.

#### Bugfixes

- A paycheck posted before its pay date now shows as paid instead of "Skipped".

#### Maintenance

- Sync server dependencies updated to fix known security vulnerabilities (express, express-rate-limit, handlebars and related packages).
- Accessibility improvements in the Paychecks section, the business calendar year preview and the mobile sync status.
- Pull requests and the development branch are scanned with Semgrep.

#### Known limitations

- Experimental.
- "Upcoming dates" in schedule and paycheck editors does not reflect skipped dates.
- Each deposit must go to a different account, and every paycheck repeats its defined amounts; edit a posted transaction for a one-off change.
- Imported deposits more than about 7.5% from the expected amount do not link automatically.
- If two paychecks are both posted before the first one's pay date, the second may show as skipped.
- The mobile business calendar editor uses the desktop editor's layout.
- Releases published on the same day may show the "What's new" message for any of them; the Notifications page lists all.

entries.details:

**Unofficial fork prerelease.** Based on Actual 26.10.0 (`2bebdbaae0b701120a8cad9d56aafd64fa04c577`); not an official Actual Budget release.

Paychecks arrive. With **Business calendars** turned on under Settings → Experimental features, "Add paycheck" on the Schedules page defines gross pay, deductions and direct deposits once, and keeps the schedules for the pay date and each deposit in step.
entries.details:
#### Features

- Define a paycheck: pay dates, gross pay and its income category, deductions to a category or as a transfer (such as a 401(k)), and direct deposits that are a fixed amount, a percent of net pay, or the remainder.
- Each paycheck books gross pay and deductions as one split transaction on the pay date in an on-budget clearing account, so the budget sees the full income and every deduction.
- Accounts get a "Business days" setting: the account's business calendar and how many business days early its direct deposits arrive.

#### Enhancements

- Each deposit is dated by its receiving account's early-deposit rule, counted in that account's calendar, and becomes a transfer from the clearing account.
- Bank-synced deposits link to their deposit schedules when the amount is close; "Post automatically" on a deposit adds it on its date instead, for manual accounts or steady amounts.
- "Skip next paycheck" skips the pay date and all its deposits together; editing, deleting and account changes keep the schedules in step, with undo.
- Saving any schedule no longer undoes a skip on schedules dated relative to it unless its dates change.

#### Bugfixes

- No fork bug fixes in this release; earlier improvements are retained.

#### Maintenance

- Record paychecks and account business days as OpenSpec specifications with tests for amounts, dates, posting, bank import matching, skipping and undo.

#### Known limitations

- Experimental and off by default; the paycheck editor is desktop only.
- Each deposit must go to a different account, and every paycheck repeats its defined amounts; edit a posted transaction for a one-off change.
- Imported deposits more than about 7.5% from the expected amount do not link automatically.

**Unofficial fork prerelease.** Based on Actual 26.10.0 (`2bebdbaae0b701120a8cad9d56aafd64fa04c577`); not an official Actual Budget release.

A schedule's date can now follow another schedule. With **Business calendars** turned on under Settings → Experimental features, choose "Relative to another schedule" as a schedule's date and set an offset, such as a deposit "2 business days before Payday".
entries.details:
#### Features

- Date a schedule relative to another schedule: a number of days or business days before or after it, counted from the other schedule's moved date.

#### Enhancements

- Business days can follow a chosen business calendar, and the result can again be moved before or after non-business days.
- Next dates, upcoming dates, account previews, posted transactions, forecasts, budget templates and transaction matching all use relative dates.
- Descriptions read, for example, "2 business days before Payday (U.S. Federal Holidays)".
- Editing the other schedule or a business calendar updates relative schedules; undo restores both.
- If the other schedule is deleted, the relative schedule shows "Source schedule was deleted" until you choose another one or delete it.

#### Bugfixes

- No fork bug fixes in this release; earlier improvements are retained.

#### Maintenance

- Record relative schedule dates as an OpenSpec specification with tests for date math, matching, previews, the schedule editor and source changes.

#### Known limitations

- Experimental and off by default.
- A relative schedule cannot be the source of another relative schedule, and offsets go up to 366.
- Skipping or posting the source schedule does not skip or post relative schedules.
- If the source schedule is deleted on another device, relative schedules there update their next dates the next time they are recomputed.
- Releases published on the same day may show the "What's new" message for any of them; the Notifications page lists all.
- Synthetic staging only; no real financial data or production paperwork migration. No iPhone acceptance test is claimed.

#### Enhancements

- Calendars are stored in the budget, sync between devices and support undo.

#### Bugfixes

#### Maintenance

- Record existing fork behavior as OpenSpec specifications and add tests for desktop note Enter handling and sync-disabled mobile status.
- Add a `business_calendars` table migration; existing budgets are unchanged until a calendar is created.
- Exclude OpenSpec-generated files from formatting checks.

#### Known limitations

- Schedules and paychecks do not use calendars yet; that arrives in later releases.
- Holidays tied to Easter must be added as yearly exceptions.

- The commit is deliberately pinned; advancing development does not silently change an existing release.
- No new iPhone acceptance test is claimed by this pipeline release.

entries.title: Release 26.10.1-alpha.2 — Ken's Actual fork
entries.body:
**Unofficial fork prerelease.** For Ken’s synthetic staging evaluation, based on Actual 26.10.0 (`2bebdbaae0b701120a8cad9d56aafd64fa04c577`). This is not an official Actual Budget release.

Desktop transaction notes now retain and expose multiple lines, including notes created on the phone. This fixes a reproduced desktop editing path that removed line breaks; the original phone-pilot incident has no client event trace establishing its exact origin.
entries.details:
#### Features

- No new product features; this release corrects transaction-note behavior.

#### Enhancements

- Show a multiline desktop note editor. Use Shift+Enter for a new line; Enter and Tab retain table navigation.
- Display the full multiline note on hover even when it fits horizontally. The transaction table retains its compact row layout.

#### Bugfixes

- Replace the single-line desktop input that stripped newlines when editing or blurring a note.
- Keep typing and arrow keys inside the multiline editor; retain beneficiary tag completion and existing quick-entry shortcuts.

#### Maintenance

- Add failing-before/fixed-after regressions for newline preservation, multiline editing and full-note previews.
- Extend browser acceptance to edit a mobile split without changing its parent or sibling, then edit the same multiline parent note on desktop.
- Align all seven package versions and Settings on `26.10.1-alpha.2` and include the desktop regressions in release CI.

#### Known limitations

- Synthetic staging only. No migration of real financial records or production paperwork.
- This release prevents the reproduced newline loss; it cannot infer missing line breaks in arbitrary historical notes.
- Automated mobile-browser checks do not replace acceptance on Ken’s installed iPhone PWA.

entries.title: Release 26.10.1-alpha.1 — Ken's Actual fork
entries.body:
**Unofficial fork prerelease.** Maintained for Ken’s synthetic staging evaluation; this is not an official Actual Budget release. Based on [Actual 26.10.0](https://actualbudget.org/blog/release-26.10.0/) (`2bebdbaae0b701120a8cad9d56aafd64fa04c577`).

This first versioned fork release improves mobile notes, receipt navigation and sync feedback, and makes the customized version visible in Settings.

- Open receipt links from mobile transaction notes without copying the URL.
- See a persistent mobile synchronization status and control.
- Preserve line breaks while editing parent and split notes.
entries.details:
#### Features

- Add a persistent mobile Sync/status bar and tappable external note links. Source: `3b1a54d`.

#### Enhancements

- Use multiline mobile parent and split note editors.
- Align the seven release packages and Settings on `26.10.1-alpha.1`; retain upstream provenance separately. Source: `cda16fb`.

#### Bugfixes

- Await refresh completion and clear the busy state after failure.
- Prefer completed sync events over cached startup connectivity after an offline launch.

#### Maintenance

- Add semantic prerelease guards and automated Settings-version acceptance.
- Verify the $901 synthetic fixture, two splits and exact IDs/notes after deployment and independent restoration.
- Publish a separate API-client maintenance artifact with asynchronous completion and sparse-split mutation fixes; this is not a new production agent service.

#### Known limitations

- Synthetic staging only; no real-budget migration or production document authorization.
- Phone receipt tapping passed. Multiline phone editing and the wider mobile pilot remain open.
- The existing demo-based mobile prefill setup remains unresolved; focused native-budget browser acceptance passes.
